head: 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e
notes: All 34 manifest files read in full against git diff b4981b8..1f725ce. A large share of style hits in this chunk are already in known.json (open rows) and were not re-reported: peekID ordering/naming/fields, startPeek params/else-if/log form, writeInstallEnv params, RunSync duplication, LoadFragment duplication and prefix, policy.go long append lines, && conditions, signature order, literals, AllowTaskContracts naming, registry save prefix, Fingerprint literals, evals regexp/nesting/doc, sessions validateScopeName placement/prefix, routines naming and the anonymous struct in TestOverrideLabels, among others. Treated as trivial variants and not raised: if/t.Errorf instead of testify in the same reworked TestOverrideLabels (covered by code-style-NIT-85-r1's rewrite), param order in policy_test.go helpers (covered by NIT-3-r2's class), and registerServerTask param order (variant of NIT-114-r1). Possible cross-chunk issue for the station: SessionIndex replaced SessionsByCwd and WorktreeCounts replaced CountWorktrees in this chunk, so callers in internal/server, which sits in another chunk, must have been migrated; this lane did not verify that.

findings.claim: The new Policy struct (7 fields, three of them slices) is passed and returned by value through every new policy function — basePolicy (63), classViolations (82), effectiveAllowlist (114), overlayViolations (143), parsePolicy (177), policyBase (195), surfaceDelta (300), CheckPolicy (329), LoadPolicy (380) — although RULE-GOLANG-POINTER-001 requires structs by pointer, by value only for small immutable value types.
findings.fix: Change the signatures to take/return *Policy (LoadPolicy/parsePolicy/basePolicy return *Policy; CheckPolicy, classViolations, effectiveAllowlist, overlayViolations, policyBase, surfaceDelta take *Policy) and update cmd/acdsl/main.go, dist.go writePolicy and the tests.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go 38-47 (Policy: AllowTaskContracts, BaseRef, DistMode, EditableScopes []string, LocalOverrides []string, Mode, VerifierAllowlist []string — not small, not immutable: writePolicy in dist.go 243-246 mutates Mode/DistMode on its copy) and every signature listed; all are new in this diff (git diff shows policy.go as a new 394-line file). No ledger row covers POINTER-001.

findings.claim: New policy.go code names its error variables resolveErr (211), readErr (248, 307), showErr (251) and baseErr (330) instead of err; RULE-GOLANG-ERR-003 requires the error variable to be named err and to shadow rather than mint xErr names.
findings.fix: Rename to err, shadowing in the if/loop scope (e.g. `if resolved, err := shellGitAbbrevRef(...); err == nil`, `content, exists, err := GitShowFile(...)`, `raw, err := os.ReadFile(...)`); at 330 use `base, isBoundary, err := policyBase(...)` and `policy, err = basePolicy(...)` at 337.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go 205-216, 244-258, 300-320, 329-340: each named variable holds an error, and each rename compiles — 248/251/307 sit in for-body blocks where := introduces new non-error names, 211 is an if-scoped init, 330 only needs 337 switched from := to =. git grep at the base shows the pattern exists elsewhere, but these lines are all new in the change (enforcement unit = added code).

findings.claim: New writePolicy names its os.Stat error statErr (255) rather than err, against RULE-GOLANG-ERR-003; err is free to shadow in that if-init scope.
findings.fix: `if _, err := os.Stat(schemaSrc); err == nil {` (the inner CopyFile `if err := ...` keeps compiling as a nested shadow).
findings.evidence: Re-read dist.go 235-261: line 255 is new in the diff; the statErr at 240 is left to the known ledger row code-style-NIT-58-r1 (whose fix deletes that stat), so only 255 is claimed here.

findings.claim: The five new git.go helpers order parameters after ctx non-alphabetically — shellGitAbbrevRef(root, ref) 26, GitChangedFiles(root, base) 46, GitMergeBase(root, ref) 69, GitRevParse(root, ref) 78, GitShowFile(root, rev, path) 89 — while RULE-GOLANG-CALL-003 requires signature parameters sorted alphabetically after ctx.
findings.fix: Reorder to (ctx, ref, root), (ctx, base, root), (ctx, ref, root), (ctx, ref, root), (ctx, path, rev, root) and update the callers in policy.go and git_test.go.
findings.evidence: Re-read git.go 24-99; all five functions are additions in this diff. The known row code-style-NIT-3-r2 covers the same class only for policy.go signatures, so git.go is a separate file-level claim.

findings.claim: New helper keepNewest(sessions, key, candidate) lists its parameters out of alphabetical order (RULE-GOLANG-CALL-003).
findings.fix: Declare keepNewest(candidate Session, key string, sessions map[string]Session) and update the two calls at 119 and 124.
findings.evidence: Re-read peek.go 117-125 and 190-197; keepNewest is new in this diff and has exactly two callers.

findings.claim: New writePolicy(root, dest string) orders its parameters non-alphabetically (RULE-GOLANG-CALL-003).
findings.fix: Declare writePolicy(dest, root string) and update Dist (106) and TestWritePolicyNoSourceShipsNothing (dist_test.go 214).
findings.evidence: Re-read dist.go 230-261 and the two call sites; writePolicy is new in this diff.

findings.claim: policyBase repeats the domain literal "origin/HEAD" (196 candidate list, 210 comparison) and hard-codes the "origin/" remote prefix (215) instead of named constants; RULE-GOLANG-CONST-001 flags a domain string repeated 2-4 times below goconst's threshold.
findings.fix: Add `const originHeadRef = "origin/HEAD"` and `const originRemotePrefix = "origin/"` and use them at 196, 210 and 215.
findings.evidence: Re-read policy.go 195-219: the 196 slice literal and the 210 comparison must agree for the abbrev-ref resolution branch to fire; both lines are new. Not covered by code-style-NIT-4-r2, which names only acdsl/policy.json and acdsl/registry.json.
